title: A Garden for the Veil Revisited
premise: Odile Vane, a temple scribe bound by debt to the Veil—a valley where magic cannot cross—has spent his life hiding the gift he was born with. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive and his found family of temple orphans is threatened, Odile flees across the Veil's boundary for the first time, discovering that the king who ordered the hunt is not a man at all but a hungry thing wearing his shape. With a disgraced hunt-captain who chose mercy and a hedge-witch exiled from her own coven, Odile journeys to the winter court to unbind the true king from the usurper. He succeeds at the cost of his own gift—spent entirely in the unbinding—and returns to the valley no longer magical, but finally free: debt forgiven, family chosen, and love declared without duty standing between.
about_author: Jude Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval herbals before turning to fiction. They write quiet fantasies about ordinary people caught in extraordinary bargains, and tend an actual garden that refuses to behave.

chapters.title: Ink That Will Not Dry
chapters.summary: POV Odile. In the temple scriptorium, Odile copies wards by day while secretly practicing small magics at night—magic that shouldn't work inside the Veil, yet does. A royal proclamation arrives: all gifted persons must be registered. Emotional beat: dread settling over routine; the first crack in his carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The temple's Abbess reveals Odile's debt was inherited from a mother who fled the valley pregnant—and that the crown's hunters have asked specifically about him. His found family of scribe-orphans quietly offers to pool their wages to buy out his contract. Emotional beat: belonging deepening just as safety collapses.

chapters.title: What the Hunters Bring
chapters.summary: POV Captain Sera Ilves. Sera, leading the hunt, recognizes the temple's head gardener as a gifted woman she once spared. Ordered to arrest the whole household, she falsifies her report instead—but her lieutenant grows suspicious. Emotional beat: conscience against career; two hunts beginning, one external, one internal.

chapters.title: Crossing the Veil
chapters.summary: POV Odile. When the lieutenant raids the temple, Odile uses his forbidden magic openly to shield the children, then flees past the valley's boundary stone—the first time magic has ever followed him instead of failing. Outside, the world blazes with enchantment, and something ancient notices him. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of becoming visible.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Exiled hedge-witch Maren catches Odile before the king's riders do and hides him in her root cellar, teaching him what his strange inside-the-Veil magic means: he is a null-born, able to touch and unravel spells. She agrees to guide him to the winter court—for a price he can't yet name. Emotional beat: wary alliance, first taste of mentorship.

chapters.title: The King Who Isn't
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Summoned to the capital, Sera attends the king's court and realizes the monarch never blinks, never eats, and smells of cold iron. Her lieutenant, now promoted, watches her for disloyalty. She defects, stealing the royal seal, and rides to intercept Odile. Emotional beat: horror crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Three Against Winter
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Sera finds Odile and Maren on the mountain road; after a knife-edge standoff, trust forms. Maren reveals the price of her help: when they unbind the king, someone null-born must hold the spell open from inside—and it will consume their gift entirely. Emotional beat: found family forged on the road, shadowed by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The usurper accelerates its plan, calling an endless winter down on the realm to starve resistance before spring. Villages freeze; refugees flood the passes. Odile, Sera, and Maren slip into the palace among them. Emotional beat: stakes made flesh—the cost of delay written in frost.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Odile. In the throne room, Odile enters the binding spell wrapped around the true king—a man imprisoned behind his own face for twenty years—and holds it open while Maren unravels it and Sera holds off the usurper's guards. The thing wearing the crown fights back through Odile's own memories. Emotional beat: climax; Odile pours every drop of his gift into the unbinding and comes out empty-handed and alive.

chapters.title: A Garden Inside the Veil
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Spring returns; the restored king pardons the hunted and voids Odile's debt. Odile goes home to the valley—powerless now, and glad of it—where the orphans, the Abbess, and Sera, newly arrived with a letter of resignation, are waiting. He plants a garden with Maren's seeds. Emotional beat: resolution; identity chosen rather than hidden, love spoken plainly, family kept.
